text.content:
Cursed Energy is negative energy and the fundamental of cursed techniques. It can be used through direct manipulation or to power innate techniques. Your Cursed Energy maximum is dependent on your class and your CE score (Wisdom or Charisma). Expended cursed energy is regained on a long rest.

Basic Cursed Energy Manipulation
There are countless applications for Cursed Energy. Your GM can allow characters to use the following to allow you to utilize cursed energy in inefficient, yet simple ways.

  • Cursed Strike. On a hit with an unarmed strike or melee weapon attack, you can spend Cursed Energy up to proficiency bonus to deal an additional d6 necrotic damage per CE.

  • Cursesight. As an action, you can make a Perception check using your CE modifier to sense cursed energy or residuals within 30 ft. The DC equals the target's CE save DC if the target was trying to conceal their cursed energy. You can track where a residual trail leads and you are aware of whose cursed energy it is if you are familiar.

Short Rest Regain
As part of a short rest you can spend up to half your maximum hit dice to regain 1 CE per Hit Dice spent.

Negative Emotion Recovery
Cursed Energy is produced by negative emotions. If you experience intense negative emotions, you might find your cursed energy responds to it. Your GM can choose to use any of these examples or create their own, regaining your proficiency bonus in CE during one of these situations. These only apply during combat when in genuine danger.

  • If you fail three ability checks or saving throws in one round.

  • If you lose half of your hit point maximum in one instance.

  • If you experience a major injury.

  • If you experience a traumatic event (GM decides) such as the loss of a friend.
Pacts made by sorcerers and given to them at birth. These pacts hold great power and even greater consequences on breaking them.

Binding Vows made for yourself and your character will be an agreement between you and your GM, you deciding what you are willing to give and the GM deciding what to give you. You can only have as many binding vows as your proficiency bonus as a rule of thumb but feel free to ignore this.

Overtime
At the cost of holding back while on the clock, when going overtime you get things done. At the cost of limiting your cursed energy during parts of the day, you can gain a bonus to your cursed energy during other parts. Your CE maximum is reduced by your CE modifier and your technique’s damage die decreases one tier from 9 AM to 5 PM.
Once this time ends, you go into Overtime. You gain temporary CE equal to twice your CE modifier and your technique’s damage die increases by two tiers. These benefits last for a number of hours equal to your proficiency bonus. Once you make this binding vow, you cannot change it until 1 workweek has passed.

Revealing One’s Hand
If you reveal your cursed technique to a creature that can understand you, you gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made using your revealed technique, as well as a bonus given by the GM that depends on their technique. This ends once combat has ended and you cannot reveal your technique to the same creature more than once or a creature that already knows your technique.

Mind Over Matter
For every limb you give up the use of, you gain a +5 bonus to your CE maximum (no prosthetics).
Immediate Activation
You need to use your cursed technique immediately, but can’t meet the usual activation requirements so you make a vow to use it without them. You create a vow to immediately use a technique that you know as either a reaction or free action just for using said technique for this vow, all other requirements besides cursed energy cost are ignored.
However, you permanently increase the action cost of the technique by 1(free action-> bonus action-> action-> full turn action) and add an additional requirement or prerequisite to use the technique for all subsequent uses of that technique (an example of an additional requirement or prerequisite would be now needing Chanting to use the technique). The increased action cost or additional requirement/prerequisite from this vow will be permanent as the technique has been permanently altered.

Favorite Enemy
You train for 1 hour preparing yourself to fight against a creature you know. You create a vow where you choose 1 creature as your "favorite enemy", after that you will choose one of the following benefits for your cursed techniques:

  • You have advantage on attack rolls against that target.

  • You reduce the target's saving throws against your techniques by your proficiency bonus.

However, any other creature besides your "favorite enemy" adds their proficiency bonus on saving throws against your cursed techniques(even if they already do), and your attack rolls will be at disadvantage against them.
Even if you take this vow multiple times you cannot choose the same creature multiple times.

Master and Servant
Requires 2+ Sorcerers
You have a deep admiration and respect for someone, so much so that you can restrain yourself just to obey them. One of the members of the vow will be the "master" of the vow, while another will be the "servant". The servant will receive one of the following restrictions:

  • Their Cursed Energy' maximum will be reduced by a number decided by its master.

  • Their technique's range is reduced by a number of ft. that the master decides.(Cannot go lower than 5ft)

  • Their technique's damage is reduced by how many damage dice the master decides.(Cannot go lower than one dice)

  • They cannot use simple domains or barriers.

The servant will have this restraint until the master allows the servant to unleash its cursed energy as an action. The servant gains one of the following benefits depending on his restraint.

  • Their cursed energy maximum doubles(using the original value without the reduction), and they regain cursed energy equal to the cursed energy they lost.

  • Their technique's range doubles(using the original value without the reduction).

  • Their technique's damage dice doubles(using the original value without the reduction).

This lasts a number of rounds equal to the master's proficiency bonus, after which this vow can only be used again after a long rest.

Taming
Requires a Sorcerer and Cursed Spirit
You can attempt to tame a cursed spirit, forcing it to obey you by means of a vow.
The cursed spirit’s CR must be equal to or lower than your proficiency bonus. You must spend 8 hours per CR to tame the cursed spirit, in 8 hour periods. During each period, you must make an Animal Handling check DC 10 + twice the CR. On a failure, you must repeat the 8 hr period.
Once you finish the process, the cursed spirit can be commanded as a bonus action. If you attack or harm the cursed spirit, the vow is broken.

Binding vows can be very powerful, especially if a player bends the rules while creating one. To help maintain balance, here is a list of binding vow concepts to watch out for:

1. Togglable Binding Vows
A player might suggest a binding vow that can be activated or deactivated at will. For example: "I am a limitless user, and I want my blue save DC to be increased by my CE modifier, but it can only affect one creature at a time. However, I can turn this vow on and off, so I don’t suffer any drawbacks."
This undermines the entire concept of binding vows because the player isn't truly sacrificing anything if they can simply toggle the effects off. For this, you can enforce a rule that it cannot be changed until completing a long rest once the vow has been made.

2. Not Actually Giving Up Anything
A player might suggest a binding vow where their melee-focused character gains advantage on all melee attack rolls but takes disadvantage on every cursed energy attack roll. Since the character isn’t reliant on CE attacks, this is not a genuine trade-off and doesn’t qualify as a fair vow.

3. More Cursed Energy Cost
A player might suggest a binding vow where they increase their cursed energy save DC in exchange for a higher cursed energy cost. While this might seem reasonable at first, it can quickly become unbalanced. Depending on the boosted feature, it could lead to encounter-ending abilities with impossibly high save DCs.

4. Reaction Negation
A player might suggest a binding vow where they lose something in return for making their cursed energy feature immune to reactions. This should be an automatic rejection, as reactions are a core mechanic of the supplement, and removing them entirely disrupts the balance of play, and completely bypasses most of the defense mechanics in the supplement.

5. Mimicry
A player might suggest a binding vow that allows their technique to mimic a feature from another technique. This should also be outright denied because it often doesn’t make logical sense and can quickly become overpowered.
6. Death Saving
A player might suggest a binding vow just as their character is about to die. For example: "I lose all my cursed energy and fall unconscious, but my technique automatically activates, teleporting me miles away." This is extremely unbalanced and effectively acts as a "get out of jail free" card, with no meaningful consequences for the player.

7. Rule Breaking
A player might suggest a binding vow that completely ignores the rules of their technique. For example: Idles transfiguration transfigured creatures being primitive or limitless being only able to teleport once per turn. The techniques rules are there for a reason and would stay better if they weren't broken by a binding vow. However sometimes a vow that breaks your techniques rules can be made good if the downside heavily outweighs the benefits.

8. Refinement Increasing
A player might suggest a binding vow that increases their domain refinement. Under no circumstances should a vow like this ever be allowed. Not only is it incredibly overpowered but it doesn't make sense lore wise, as binding vows can only be used to amplify a sorcerer’s physicals, their cursed technique, or cursed energy in some sort of way, and the refinement of a barrier is based only on your expertise in putting one together.

9. Metagaming
A player might suggest a binding vow that their character couldn't possibly know about. For example: A character that doesn't have a barrier feat or levels in the Support Specialist class, making a binding vow for a complex binding vow for a barrier. For example: I vow that my barrier is reverse triangle shaped and any objects with cursed energy imbued into them can't pass through it at a certain time of the day but the HP of the barrier is reduced by 30 every round and it's cursed energy cost is increased by half of the original cost, despite not having any advanced barrier knowledge.

pages.name: Consequences of Breaking a Binding Vow

text.content:
A consequence feared by all from the weakest to the strongest. All sorcerers follow one rule; “Do not break a binding vow.”

After breaking a multi binding vow, you lose any benefits from the vow, and either gain 5 levels of exhaustion for 10 days or a major misfortune falls upon you, rolling on the table below.

Roll Misfortune
1 Death.
2 You lose a limb.
3 You lose a sense(D4: 1.Touch, 2. Taste, 3. Smell, 4. Sight)
4 Your stats are reduced by 2.
5 You cannot use Cursed Energy for 8d4 days.
6 Your Innate Technique is confiscated for 6d4 days.

The punishments can be avoided if both parties agree to end the vow.
Events reached either during extreme focus or moments near death, you manage to glimpse the core of cursed energy. Breakthroughs take one of two forms.

Channeling cursed energy into an attack within 0.000001, you cause a spatial distortion where cursed energy sparks black. This event is called a black flash.

In order to land a black flash, you must land a critical hit. After landing a critical hit, you roll a second d20, on a natural 20 you activate a black flash. This causes the melee attack to deal triple critical damage, rolling 3x the dice instead of 2x and ignore damage resistances.

Wish whoosh, reverse cursed technique processes negative energy into positive energy by taking two sources of cursed energy and multiplying them by one other. Impossible to teach normally.

After almost dying, be it being reduced to 0 in one hit while at max HP, or failing two death saves and then rolling a nat 20. Those are moments where the GM can choose to bestow reverse cursed technique. Alternatively roll a d100, on a 90+ you gain Reverse Cursed Technique. Reverse Cursed Technique cannot be taught under any circumstances, not including extremely specific outliers like Soul Swap.

You learn to use your cursed energy in a completely opposite way, channeling positive energy instead of negative. You have a pool of healing you can use with your reverse cursed energy that's equal to 5 x your level x your Cursed Energy modifier. As a bonus action for cursed energy up to your CE Modifier, you can remove healing from that pool to regain hit points. You can also remove healing from the pool as a reaction to receiving damage once per round. For every 1 cursed energy spent, you regain 10 hit points, removing an equal amount from the pool. If you are suffering from a physical condition or injury such as a concussion or something else, one of these effects can be healed for every 10 hit points recovered with the reverse cursed technique. Limbs can be regenerated for 20 hit points.

You can use your Reverse Cursed Technique until your healing pool ends before getting burned out, during which you can't use RCT until your healing pool recovers. At the beginning of every two rounds, your healing pool recovers 10 hit points. Your healing pool automatically refills at the end of a long rest. You can remove maximum HP reductions from Soul Damage by spending healing if you have at least 6 levels of Soul Awareness.

The awakened state following a breakthrough causes a sorcerer to gain an increased understanding of their cursed energy. When a character lands a black flash or awakens reverse cursed technique, your DM can allow the following upgrades as your ability to use cursed energy improves dramatically (counting total Breakthroughs).

Skilled Cursed Energy Manipulation
Prerequisite: 16+ Cursed Energy score, 1 Breakthrough

You have focused on the basics, allowing you to directly manipulate cursed energy to great effect.

  • Cursed Strike. On a hit, you can spend up to your proficiency bonus, dealing an additional d8 necrotic damage per CE spent.

  • Cursed Reinforcement. As an action you can spend up to your Cursed Energy modifier to reinforce your body. You gain 5 temporary hit points per CE.

Advanced Cursed Energy Manipulation
Prerequisite: Skilled Cursed Energy Manipulation, 4 Breakthroughs

You have perfected the basics of manipulating cursed energy, causing your effectiveness and efficiency to explode.

  • Cursed Strike. On a hit, you can spend up to your proficiency bonus, dealing an additional 1d12 necrotic damage per CE spent.

  • Cursed Reinforcement. As an action, bonus action, or reaction you can spend up to your Cursed Energy modifier + proficiency to reinforce your body. You gain 5 temporary hit points per CE.

  • Efficiency. When using a cursed technique, the base cost decreases by 1 (min cost of 1).

Mastered Cursed Energy Manipulation
Prerequisite: Advanced Cursed Energy Manipulation, 8 Breakthroughs

  • Cursed Strike. On a hit, you can spend up to your proficiency bonus, dealing an additional 2d8 necrotic damage per CE. Additionally, you can spend CE up to your proficiency to add to your attack roll.

  • Efficiency. When using a cursed technique, the base cost decreases by 2 (min cost of 1).

Positive Energy is poisonous to a Cursed Spirit which removes their ability to ever use Reverse Cursed Technique. Cursed Spirits have an easier time healing directly with negative energy using Cursed Energy Affinity, but they are quickly overwhelmed by the difference in output.
When a Cursed Spirit would normally unlock Reverse Cursed Technique, they instead gain an understanding unique to curses. They gain a number of Profane Points equal to their level and gain an additional point when they gain a level. At any time, you can spend any number of Profane Points you possess to gain a Cursed Physiology Attribute. Each Attribute has an individual cost and can only be taken once unless stated otherwise.

Ability Improvement (1 point)
You gain a +1 to an ability score of your choice. You can choose this attribute multiple times, but only once for every 3 levels you have (E.g. level 9 can only have 3 Ability Improvement attributes).

Darkvision (1 point)
you have superior vision in dark and dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray. This increases to 120 feet at 8th level.

Increased Speed (1 point)
Whether you are quadruped or have strong legs, your walking speed increases by 5 ft. This increases by 5 ft again at 10th level.

Horrifying Form (1 point)
You are a terrifying curse and a horror to behold. You gain proficiency in Intimidation or expertise if you are already proficient.

Ambush Predator (1 point)
You gain proficiency in either Stealth, Deception, Perception, or Survival.
Curse Weapon (1 point)
You gain a natural weapon that takes the form of claws (slashing), fangs (piercing), or gnarled fists or a tail (bludgeoning). Your Curse Weapon deals 1d6 + your Strength modifier of its damage type. This increases to 1d8 at 5th level and 1d10 at 10th level. If you have a different unarmed strike dice, you can choose to use that for these natural weapons. You can choose this attribute multiple times, but must choose a different option each time.

Curse Weapon: Claw (2 points)
Once per turn when you hit a creature with a claw attack, you can force the creature to take a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier). On a failed save, the target bleeds and takes 1d4 slashing damage at the start of their next turn. This increases to 1d6 slashing damage at 10th level. You can spend 1 CE to make the extra damage necrotic. You must have the Cursed Weapon attribute and choose claw to take this attribute.

Curse Weapon: Fangs (2 points)
Once per turn when you hit a creature with a fang attack, you can force the creature to take a Strength saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier). On a failed save, the target is dragged down and falls prone. You must have the Cursed Weapon attribute and choose fang to take this attribute.

Curse Weapon: Gnarled Fist (2 points)
The bludgeoning damage of your gnarled fists become 1d8. This increases to 1d10 at 5th level and 1d12 at 10th level. Once per turn when you hit a creature with a gnarled fists attack, you can force the creature to take a Strength saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier). On a failed save, the target is pushed back 10 ft. If the target impacts a solid object or structure, it takes 1d4 bludgeoning damage. This increases to 15 ft at 5th level and the bludgeoning damage increases to 2d4 at 10th level. You must have the Cursed Weapon attribute and choose gnarled fist to take this attribute.

Cursed Weapon: Tail (2 points)
The reach of your tail increases to 10 ft. As a reaction to an attack roll, you can swipe your tail to roll a 1d6 and add it to your AC against the triggering attack, potentially causing it to miss. You can spend 1 CE to add a +2 to the number rolled. This becomes +4 at 10th level. You must have the Cursed Weapon attribute and choose tail to take this attribute.
Poisonous Weapon (2 points)
Once per turn when you hit a creature with a natural weapon, you can spend 1 CE to force the target to make a Constitution saving throw (DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution or CE modifier). On a failed save, the target takes 2d4 poison damage and is poisoned until the start of your next turn. The damage becomes 3d4 at 6th level and 4d4 at 12th level. You must have the Cursed Weapon attribute to choose this attribute.

Greater Cursesight (2 points)
You gain a +2 bonus to ability checks to detect cursed energy. This bonus increases by +1 at 5th, 8th, 12th, and 16th level.

Powerful Build (2 points)
You count as 1 size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift.

Additional Limbs (3 points)
Arm. You have an additional arm somewhere on your body. The additional arm can manipulate an object, open or close a door or container, pick up or set down a Tiny object, or wield a weapon that has the light property. This does not give you additional attacks, but does give you a +2 bonus on ability checks to grapple a creature.
Leg. You have an additional leg somewhere on your body. This leg gives you a +2 bonus on ability checks and saving throws against being knocked prone or moved against your will. Your walking speed increases by 5 ft per additional leg you have when you take the dash action.
You can take this attribute multiple times, up to a total of four times.

Size Increase (4 points)
Your size increases by one size category up to Gargantuan. This causes a +2 increase to your Strength score and -2 penalty to your Dexterity score. Additionally, your unarmed strikes and natural weapons increase by one dice tier up to d12 (d4<d8<d10<d12). You can take this attribute multiple times with stacking benefits, but the cost increases by 2 every time.

Flight (6 points)
You sprout grotesque wings that give you a 30 ft fly speed. To use this speed, you cannot be wearing heavy armor or carrying more than your carry capacity. If you also have the Greater Flight Improvement attribute, you gain the Evasion feature while flying.
Flight Improvement (3 points)
Your fly speed can equal your walking speed if it is higher. You must have the Flight attribute to take this attribute.

Greater Flight Improvement (4 points)
You gain a 30 ft fly speed that allows you to hover, so being stunned or knocked prone will not cause you to fall. If you are wearing heavy armor or carrying more than your carry capacity this speed is halved. If you do not have the Flight attribute, the cost of this feature increases by 3 points.

Cursed Inventory (3 points)
You have learned to store items within your body, which cannot normally be removed against your will unless you die. You can store objects that could reasonably fit within your body. Additionally, your carry capacity increases by 3 x your level. The total weight you can store in your body equals half your carry capacity.

Multiple Eyes (3 points)
You have countless grotesque eyes on your body. You have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

Alternate Movement (3 points)
You gain either a 10 ft burrow speed, a 30 ft climb speed, or a 30 ft swim speed. You can choose this attribute multiple times, but must choose a different option each time.

Alternate Movement Improvement (2 points)
Your climb or swim speed can equal your walking speed if it is higher. Your burrow speed increases to 10 ft and becomes 15 ft at 10th level. You must have the Alternate Movement attribute to take this. You can choose this attribute multiple times, but must choose a different option each time.

Cursed Armor (4 points)
You have strong scales or plating that protect you from harm. You gain a +2 bonus to AC.
Offensive Output (4 points)
When you use Cursed Strike, you deal an additional 1 necrotic damage per CE spent. If a feature alters the damage type of your cursed energy, it also changes this damage. This increases to 2 damage per CE spent at 10th level.

Shifting Form (4 points)
Your body lacks a conventional structure. You can move through spaces as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing, provided you aren't wearing or carrying anything you cannot fit through. You also have advantage on saving throws against being grappled or restrained.

General Understanding (5 points)
You gain 1 Physical or Skill Feat of your choice that you qualify for. You can take this attribute multiple times, but must choose a different feat each time.

Cursed Energy Understanding (6 points)
You gain 1 Cursed Energy Feat of your choice that you qualify for. You can take this attribute multiple times, but must choose a different feat each time.

Technique Understanding (8 points)
You gain 1 Innate Technique Feat that you qualify for. You can take this attribute multiple times, but must choose a different feat each time.

Greater Affinity (8 points)
Your Cursed Energy Affinity feature is replaced by the Increased Affinity feature.

Domain Expansion is the most supreme technique of any jujutsu user. It is achieved by expanding one's innate domain with cursed energy while using a barrier to construct it inside a separate space. The caster then imbues their cursed technique within the barrier to complete the expansion, allowing them to deploy their ability all throughout the domain.

All domains are different from each other, varying in their hand signs or techniques. However, they all tend to follow the same base rules unless otherwise stated.

Expanding Your Domain
All domains require a specific hand sign for their expansion to be activated, taking a Full Turn Action (Action + Bonus Action + Movement) to activate. All domains cost 20 Cursed Energy unless specified, and trap all creatures of your choice in a 175-foot radius circle centered on you, creating a barrier for 1 minute. The insides of a domain expansion vary from user to user, since it's like showing your soul to your opponents. Outside of your domain, its appearance is of a giant black sphere floating in the air.

All creatures outside your domain will receive Xd6 bludgeoning damage(X = CE modifier) and be pushed to the edge of the barrier. They received an additional 1d4 bludgeoning damage per object they collided with as the domain pushed them. In case the domain forces them against a wall, they must start holding their breath until the domain is closed or shrunk. Your barrier has domain hit points equal to 10 x your CE modifier, AC equal to 10 + your CE modifier + 1 per 100 refinement, and is vulnerable to damage from the outside and resistant to damage from the inside. Work with your GM to determine the environment and terrain of your domain.

Technique Burnout
Even if the barrier or environment isn't fully formed, casting domain expansion causes the user's innate technique to become unstable for a short time afterward. Right after ending your domain expansion, you cannot use any innate technique features and gain 2 levels of exhaustion for 1 minute or until you land a black flash.

Domains that are expanded to be lethal are constructed within a barrier imbued with the user's cursed technique. The caster's abilities are amplified and any cursed techniques deployed within the domain are guaranteed to hit their target. This sure-hit factor is derived from the barrier's embedded technique, which is what makes this type of domain considered lethal.

Sure Hit Effect
While inside your domain radius, all of your innate techniques will be affected by a sure hit effect. No matter what your cursed energy attack roll is, it will be considered a hit. Creatures will automatically fail saving throws for your innate technique. This and any other effects of your domain only apply to targets that you choose inside it.

In the past, Domain Expansion was a more common technique because domains weren't constructed to be fatal. They only forced targets inside to obey the rules of the embedded cursed technique. In exchange for lacking a guaranteed hit, a Non-Lethal Domain has one of the following:

Peace Treaty
While inside Non-Lethal domains, no kinds of violence or harmful action is allowed while a condition is not completely followed through. After the condition is completed, the domain will end.

Anti-Domain Clash
Because your domain has a peaceful condition, you cannot open it while another domain expansion is active, however lethal domain expansions cannot be opened as a reaction to your domain opening. You can use your reaction to open your domain against a lethal domain, in which case the clash is different. The domain with more refinement points instantly destroys the other. In the case of two non-lethal domains opening, the one with more refinement points will instantly win.

As with every technique, Domain Expansion gets better with refinement and specialization. A refined domain and a normal domain are very different, while in the second case, most semi-grade 1 or above sorcerers could escape, a refined domain can bring trouble to even special-grade sorcerers.

Refinement Points
The longer you refine your domain, the more refinement points you have. You start out with 1 refinement point, which defines many things about your domain. Your refinement limit is 1000 refinement points, only the elite of the elite have ever reached said point.

Refinement Benefits
The more you refine your domain, the more versatile you can make it. Depending on your refinement points, you gain the following:

Benefit Description Refinement
Domain Durability Your domain will increase in its durability the more refined it is. Your domain hit points are increased by +1 per refinement point you have. 1+
Barrier Resistance The stronger the barrier of a domain on the inside, the weaker it is on the outside. You have realized this, and have found ways to get around it. As part of expanding your domain, you can decide if you want to make your barrier have vulnerability on the inside in exchange for it being resistant to all damage on the outside. In addition, you can spend additional 5 cursed energy when expanding your domain to make it perfectly balanced, making both outside and inside have no vulnerabilities or immunities. 100
Quicker Expansion Through training, you have learned how to use your domain hand signs with more efficiency. Your domain now costs an action instead of a Full-Turn Action. 200
Increased Potency While inside your domain, your techniques are at their strongest. While inside your domain, your cursed techniques and domain damage if any have additional dice equal to your Cursed Energy modifier. 300
0.2 Second Expansion You have learned how to expand your domain so quickly that almost no one can react to it. As part of opening your domain, you can make it last only until the end of your turn. The cost for this domain expansion is halved, and it cannot be reacted to unless the creature has a higher Dexterity score than your CE score. When opening your domain this way, all creatures are targeted by its effects, too fast to choose. 400
Lasting Domain With great practice, you have learned how to make your domain last far longer than it normally would. Your domain now lasts for 2 minutes instead of 1. 500
Domain Amplification You have learned how to utilize the power of a domain without actively using it. As an action for half as much Cursed Energy your domain requires, you can cover your body to "wear" your domain in order to neutralize cursed techniques for 1 minute. Once activated, you automatically negate any defensive technique, offensive technique, or spell that affects you, and you can bypass barriers such as infinity with melee attacks. You will also negate a domain's sure hit effect if you're inside one. In addition, you can not use your Innate Technique unless you dismiss Domain Amplification as a bonus action. Even if you dismiss it, for the minute you can reactivate it as a bonus action without spending the cursed energy again. This technique does not work against techniques on Maximum Output if the user has 51 or more higher refinement than you. If they are within 50 refinement of you, you have resistance to their technique, and if they have 51 or less refinement than you, you are immune to their techniques even if they use Maximum Output. 600
Efficient Expansions It is no secret that opening and maintaining a domain is a very complicated job, requiring lots of cursed energy quantity, practice, and refinement. You have refined this with training, reducing your domain expansion cost by your Cursed Energy modifier. In addition, you only gain 1 level of exhaustion after your domain. 700
Durable Barrier Your domain barrier has become hard and quite unbreakable, making escape or forced entry almost impossible. Your domain will gain immunity to non-magical damage from both sides, however, it will still be resistant to all damages from the inside and vulnerable to all damages from the outside. In addition, your domain's refinement points are doubled when calculating your domain's hit points. 800
Compression You have found a method to make your domain take up less space while making it harder to hit from the outside. As a bonus action while on your domain, you can spend 5 cursed energy to compress it, making the outside become a small circle of 5ft. Inside, however, will be the same size. Attack rolls against your domain on the outside are made with disadvantage, while barrierless domains must use this feature to target your domain on the outside. This lasts until the end of the domain. 900
Total Mastery You have reached the pinnacle of Jujutsu, mastering domain expansion. You have mastered your domain hand signs and can expand your domain as a bonus action instead of an action. You can reduce your domain expansion's cost by your proficiency bonus. While inside the domain, techniques that use an action can now be used as a bonus action, and techniques that take a bonus action can be used as a free action. Your domain now lasts for 3 minutes. 1000

If you have RCT and Domain Refinement of 750 or higher, you gain:
Burnout Recovery. You have realized the complicated issue of Technique Burnout can be solved in a simple fashion. Substitute your brain for a new one! Whilst under the effects of Technique Burnout, you can spend 4 cursed energy as a reaction to regain your Cursed Technique and remove the exhaustion from Burnout. You must succeed on a DC 5 Constitution saving throw. On a success, you remove Burnout without major consequences. On a failure, your eyes and nose start to bleed profusely as you take 8d6 psychic damage and cannot take actions or bonus actions until the start of your next turn. The Constitution saving throw DC increases by 5 for every success, being reduced by 5 for every minute that passes and resets on a long rest.
Methods of Refinement
There are multiple ways of refining your domain, from training with yourself to clashing with other people's domains. Below is to list of how to gain refinement points:

Method Description Rewards
Training Probably the slowest method, but every little progress counts. Once per day, you can spend a number of Cursed Energy up to your Cursed Energy modifier to add to your refinement level. This Cursed Energy can only be regained the next day. X
Domain Casualties One of the quicker methods of refining your domain is to destroy opponents with your cursed techniques while inside it. If you reduce a creature to 0 hit points while it's inside your domain expansion, you will gain refinement points. The refinement points are only gained if the creature's CR was at least half of your level(rounded up). 20/Creature
Domain Superiority Subjugate another with your own. If you win in a domain clash, you gain refinement points from your domain superiority. You can only benefit from this once per month and not against the same creature. 100 Points

All kinds of barriers have a weak spot, domain expansions could not be different. You can only deal damage to a domain's hit points once you've found its weak spot unless you're outside the domain.

From Inside
Breaking a barrier from the inside is almost impossible, even if you do find the weak point of the barrier you'll still be targeted by the domain's constant effects. To break a domain from the inside, you must find its weak spot first by making a DC 30 Perception check. On a failure, the target cannot find a weak spot. On a success, you will find the domain's weak spot, now being able to target it for your attacks. The barrier has resistance to damage when attacked from inside.

From Outside
While breaking a barrier from inside is nearly impossible, breaking from the outside is a much easier task. You can normally target the domain with attacks. It automatically fails any saving throws, and is vulnerable to all damage other than psychic.

Forming a Weak Spot
Sometimes, even though it may seem like a disadvantage, you can forcefully enter a domain expansion by creating a weak spot, generally a hole of some sort. After you have reached at least 1/3rd of the domain's maximum hit points, you can take an action to make a Strength, Charisma, or Wisdom saving throw to forcefully open the domain. On a success, you will form a 10 ft by 10 ft hole in the domain that allows you and any creatures to enter inside the domain while you are concentrating. The moment any creature enters the domain they suffer the effects of the sure-hit.

When a creature expands its domain, you can use your reaction to expand your own domain as well. The domain battle will be defined by the one with the most refinement points, being the defining factor in deciding the winner. However, even if you do have refinement points to destroy the opposing domain it will take a number of rounds equal to the amount of refinement points that you have above the opponent's domain. The domain clash creates a 350 foot area, where 175 feet of it will be within one domain's area while the other 175 feet is for the other’s domain. The loser's domain area will shrink by 15 ft per round passed. Once you break the enemy’s domain, your sure-hit effect immediately resumes.

Equal Refinement Clash
Although an extremely unlikely scenario. When two Domain Expansions of equal refinement clash, they completely nullify each other, not being able to overpower or be overpowered, so it's up to the two sorcerers to maintain their domain while bringing the opponent's down. As soon as one of the domain casters reach 1/3 (rounded down) of their maximum hit points they need to succeed in a DC 15 roll with no modifiers to maintain concentration on their domain. On a success, the domain is kept stable and they can keep going. On a failure, their domain breaks, giving in to the opponent's, and they suffer the after effects of Burnout from Domain Expansion.

Multiple Domain Clashes
A battle of two domain expansions is already hard to describe, now one of three or more is simply chaotic. When three or more domains are involved, the rules are the same, with the domains with less refinement being destroyed as soon as the necessary rounds pass. The barrier is expanded by 175 ft per domain involved, with the weaker domains getting reduced by 15 feet at the beginning of each round.

You have refined your domain expansion to new levels, making it become a true work of art. This can only be achieved by experiencing a breakthrough after reaching 1000 refinement points.

On a failure, the domain is destroyed. Your techniques still have a sure hit effect, however due to not having a barrier your domain is much simpler to escape. Also on a domain clash, your domain effects and cursed techniques can target the outside barrier of the other domain directly.
